title: What running a tiny live account taught me that paper trading never showed
author: Tasty-Mammoth5321

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: shadow accounts for the trades the agent rejects is the smartest part of this. most people only ever see what their filter let through.

replies.author: Tasty-Mammoth5321
replies.body: Thanks, that part ended up mattering more than I expected. Mostly the rejected trades lose, which quietly backs the skips, but now and then one group of them does not, and that is what made me revisit a single threshold. The catch is that a shadow account is optimistic: mine fills at the signal price with a fixed fee and no queue or market impact, so I treat it as an upper bound. Do you track your rejects too, and if so, how do you handle the fill assumptions?

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: I do, and fill at the signal price is the bit I'd distrust first. for options I fill buys at the ask and sells at the bid, never the middle, so rejects don't look better than they were. I built Quantradin (quantradin.com) around that, free and paper only. for stocks I'd at least push the fill to the next bar's open.

replies.author: Tasty-Mammoth5321
replies.body: That is fair, and it is on my list. Buying at the ask and selling at the bid is the honest convention, and my shadow account does not do it yet, which is exactly why I call it an upper bound. For the stock side I am already leaning toward the next bar's open instead of the signal price. Do you add a small delay on top of that for the decision itself?

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: I do, one bar. the rule only sees the closed bar and the fill is the open of the next one, so it can never act on a price it only saw after the fact. on daily bars that's plenty, on 1 min bars I'd still add a second or two for the order itself.

comments.author: QATSAlgo
comments.body:
The accidental test orders are a useful recovery case to preserve: a test process should fail closed before it has an execution-capable connection, and a timeout should remain “unknown” until reconciled. For the shadow accounts, keep signal time and the first executable price separate so rejected trades don’t receive an unrealistically favourable fill.



We’re QATS. If you want to try a separate prop-perpetuals adapter, our API docs cover account-bound connections, account/risk state, idempotency keys and command confirmation: [https://quantityproject.github.io/qats-trader-api/](https://quantityproject.github.io/qats-trader-api/) . QATS evaluations and initial funded accounts are simulated; they are a distinct plan-governed environment, not an exchange testnet or proof that live fills will match.
